name: Intel
thesis: Once the undisputed king of chips, Intel lost the AI/data centre race entirely to NVIDIA and AMD. Manufacturing fell behind TSMC by 2+ node generations. Lost Apple (switched to ARM in 2020), lost server share to AMD EPYC, and missed the GPU moment. Pat Gelsinger fired Dec 2024 after turnaround stalled. IDM 2.0 strategy (in-house foundry + external customers) burning cash with no clear revenue timeline.
keyRisks: Continued market share loss to AMD in PC/server; Intel Foundry Services losing customers; pension-like capex burden; management instability post-Gelsinger.
catalysts: Intel 18A node if it achieves yield parity with TSMC; US CHIPS Act funding (.5B) backstop; potential M&A (Qualcomm, Apollo rumoured); AI PC cycle (Core Ultra Meteor Lake/Arrow Lake) if it accelerates.

name: PayPal
thesis: PayPal was the dominant online checkout brand for 20 years. Apple Pay, Google Pay, Stripe, and Shop Pay have structurally eroded the moat. Branded checkout losing share even as total payment volume grows. New CEO Alex Chriss (from Intuit) executing cost cuts and refocusing on branded checkout but the competitive environment is permanently harder. Stock down 80%+ from 2021 peak.
keyRisks: Continued share loss in checkout to Apple/Google/Stripe; Venmo failing to monetise; losing PayPal's "default" checkout position as merchants consolidate onto fewer processors.
catalysts: Branded checkout stabilisation; Venmo monetisation via debit card + PayPal Everywhere; AI fraud detection as a premium service; potential BNPL (Buy Now Pay Later) recovery.

name: Disney
thesis: Disney over-invested in streaming (Disney+) at the expense of its parks and studio margins. B+ annual streaming losses 2020-2023. ESPN cord-cutting secular decline. Bob Iger returned but faces a structural media transition — linear TV still generates most profits while it slowly decays. Parks remain exceptional but China park underperforms.
keyRisks: ESPN linear TV decline accelerating; Disney+ churn as password sharing crackdown plateaus; studio slate misses (lack of Marvel/Pixar hits); theme park capex cycle.
catalysts: Disney+ profitability milestone (achieved Q4 2024); ESPN direct-to-consumer launch; legacy IP revitalisation (new Toy Story, Avengers, Star Wars); India (Hotstar) growth.

name: Nike
thesis: Nike over-indexed on DTC (direct to consumer) digital, cut wholesale partners, and missed the performance running trend (On Running, Hoka, New Balance all took share). Fired John Donahoe, brought back Elliott Hill. Inventory glut forced heavy discounting, damaging brand. Revenue declined for 3 consecutive quarters. Cultural relevance declining among younger consumers.
keyRisks: On Running / Hoka permanently taking running market share; brand fatigue among Gen Z; wholesale rebuilding takes 2+ years; China recovery slower than expected.
catalysts: Elliott Hill turnaround: rebuilding wholesale, cutting SKUs, innovation pipeline (Air Max Dn, Pegasus Premium); Olympics 2028; Jordan Brand / lifestyle stability; China recovery.

name: Boeing
thesis: Two 737 MAX crashes (2018-2019), COVID grounding all production, and an Alaska Airlines door-plug blowout (Jan 2024) have made Boeing a case study in quality management failure. 15 straight years of Dreamliner production problems. B in debt. FAA production caps limiting output. Kelly Ortberg (new CEO Sep 2024) inheriting a broken manufacturing culture. The Airbus duopoly means Boeing cannot be allowed to fail — but recovery is 3-5 year minimum.
keyRisks: Additional safety incidents triggering more FAA caps; machinists union strikes (happened Sep 2024); cash burn rate (B in 2024); 737 MAX reputational damage with airlines; China delivery backlog.
catalysts: FAA production cap removal for 737 MAX 10; 777X certification; Kelly Ortberg culture reset; B+ equity raise completion; strong commercial backlog (B) once production normalises.

name: Starbucks
thesis: Starbucks grew too fast, lost its third-place experience identity, and got caught between premium (competing with independent specialty cafes) and value (competition from McDonald's McCafe, Dutch Bros). Mobile app order overload slowed service quality. China segment structurally pressured by Luckin Coffee. Brian Niccol hired from Chipotle (Sep 2024) as a turnaround catalyst.
keyRisks: Niccol turnaround slower than expected; China never recovering to pre-2023 levels; labour costs staying elevated; mobile order complexity throttling throughput.
catalysts: Brian Niccol back-to-basics: simpler menu, better barista experience, mobile app fixes; Morning Daypart recapture; licensed stores (airports, hospitals) outperforming; China stabilisation.

name: Pfizer
thesis: Pfizer made B from COVID vaccines/Paxlovid (2021-2022), then revenues collapsed 40%+ as demand normalised. Spent B acquiring Seagen (oncology) to fill the post-COVID gap, piling on debt. Pipeline disappointments (obesity drug failure vs Eli Lilly/Novo lead) hurt sentiment. Stock down 60%+ from 2021 peak. Albert Bourla under pressure.
keyRisks: GLP-1 (obesity) pipeline failure vs Lilly/Novo; Paxlovid volume permanently lower; Seagen integration costs; patent cliffs on Eliquis/Ibrance 2026-2028.
catalysts: Oncology pipeline from Seagen (Adcetris + 9 other approved drugs); RSV vaccine Abrysvo global rollout; cost cuts (B programme); potential re-rating if obesity pipeline delivers.

name: Zoom Video
thesis: Zoom became a verb during COVID — then Microsoft Teams, bundled free with Office 365, systematically eroded its enterprise base. Revenue growth went from 326% (2021) to near-zero. Enterprise transition happening but slow. Now pivoting to AI Companion (meeting summaries, AI notetaker) and Zoom Phone to move up the stack. Trading at ~12x FCF — cheap if AI products gain traction.
keyRisks: Microsoft Teams bundling permanently capping enterprise upside; consumer base churning; commoditisation of video conferencing; AI Companion not differentiating enough.
catalysts: Zoom AI Companion monetisation; Zoom Phone as UCaaS platform; enterprise cross-sell; potential M&A target (Salesforce, ServiceNow speculation); FCF yield attractive for buybacks.

name: 3M
thesis: 3M spun off its healthcare business (Solventum) May 2024 and is now fighting .5B in Combat Arms earplug litigation settlements plus .3B in PFAS (forever chemical) water contamination settlements. New CEO William Brown refocusing on industrial operations but litigation overhangs persist. Once a Buffett-style compounder, now a value trap debate.
keyRisks: PFAS liability could exceed current .3B settlement; Combat Arms settlement payment schedule straining cash flow; restructuring costs post-Solventum spin.
catalysts: PFAS and earplug liabilities fully quantified and resolved; William Brown operational improvement; abrasives/adhesives / auto businesses re-rated on standalone basis; dividend sustainability confirmed.
